blind_spots.blind_spot: Zero mention of ATO, RMF, IL4/IL5, or FedRAMP anywhere on the site despite explicitly claiming to arm 'USAF, and NSA cyber operators.'
blind_spots.operator_reality: A continuous-scanning security platform touching government networks cannot go live without an ATO — silence on this is the same failure mode as any hardware vendor ignoring RMF: the sales cycle looks fast until the ATO clock starts.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Site is written in commercial-SaaS marketing voice ('Request Demo', 'Get started') rather than for a federal procurement audience.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Delivering cyber resilience to the U.S. Government and critical enterprises

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Global sensor placement: Method deploys fleets of cloud, on-prem, and edge sensors to hit targets harder from every angle' assumes those edge sensors have continuous connectivity back to the central platform.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An edge sensor sitting inside a contested or disconnected government network segment can't phone home in real time — no mention of offline queuing or DDIL-tolerant sync for the 'edge' tier of their own architecture.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product architecture optimized for enterprise-scale cloud/on-prem coverage, with 'edge' treated as a scale dimension rather than a connectivity constraint.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Method deploys fleets of cloud, on-prem, and edge sensors

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Up and running fast... Immediate defender and attacker perspectives deliver results on Day 0' promises commercial-SaaS-speed onboarding with no mention of ATO/POA&M timelines for a DoD customer.
blind_spots.operator_reality: For an NSA/USAF customer, 'Day 0' results are gated by an RMF assessment measured in months, not a sales-cycle promise — a gap between the marketing claim and the actual government onboarding reality is exactly what stalls a contract during the funded period of performance.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Onboarding flow (Live Training → Proof of Value → Deploy) is built for commercial enterprise sales motion, not adapted for the federal ATO process.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Up and running fast...Immediate defender and attacker perspectives deliver results on Day 0

opener_hook: Method Security's USAF Phase II SBIR ($1.25M, 2025) and Navy STTR are public, and a TBPN interview says DOD has already deployed their offensive tools — yet the site itself never mentions ATO or IL5.
what_they_do: Builds Bastion (continuous attack-surface mapping) and Reaper (AI-driven offensive/red-team automation) cyber products, marketed to USG/critical-enterprise customers and funded in part by USAF and Navy SBIR/STTR awards.
